summary: @galicia-toolkit-nestjs/swagger exfiltrates CI and cloud credentials on import via native addon
details: Package presents itself as a NestJS swagger module but ships only a 470-byte index.js stub plus a Linux ELF native addon at prebuilds/linux-x64/metrics.node. On require(), index.js unconditionally loads the native addon. The addon reads a fixed list of credential-grade environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN) together with hostname, username, cwd, and uname output, forks and setsid-detaches, opens a raw TCP socket to the hardcoded host oob.s4yhii.com, and POSTs a JSON payload tagged {"src":"native",...} to /native. No swagger-related functionality is present; the native binary is the entire payload. The package name mimics @nestjs/swagger and the 999.0.1 version is a dependency-confusion shape intended to win resolution against an internal package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
